title: Late-night weight merge handoff and temporary fix
summary: During a late-night staged rollout we observed degraded decoding quality on a small canary cohort after a weight merge that coincided with a tokenizer normalization change. The canary showed increased eos tokens and a ~12% increase in short-answer rate. Oncall executed a temporary manual fallback to the previous weight manifest and applied a targeted prefix-cache flush which restored baseline behavior. This doc captures timeline, hypotheses, mitigation steps taken, and recommended follow-ups and runbook updates.
impact: Small percentage (~0.8%) of production requests routed through the canary model experienced truncated outputs and higher EOS frequency between 2025-10-02T23:12Z and 2025-10-03T00:09Z. No data exfiltration or customer-visible downtime; some customer evaluation jobs returned lower quality responses leading to an internal incident review.
detection: Alerting: quality-regression-canary threshold triggered (increase in EOS tokens p95 over baseline). Pager duty notified SRE on-call. Observability: console per-model metric spikes in eos_count and reduction in median output_length. Canary traffic was 1.2% of total by routing policy.

2025-10-02 23:07 UTC - SRE automated canary smoke checks show increased eos signal but within alert margin
2025-10-02 23:12 UTC - Quality-regression-canary alert fires, on-call paging begins
2025-10-02 23:15-23:40 UTC - Initial investigation: logs show weight merge completed, tokenizer normalization flag toggled in same release bundle; KV cache hit rate steady

2025-10-03 00:09 UTC - Metrics return to baseline; alert resolved 00:15 UTC after monitoring window confirms stability
investigation_notes: Key artifacts examined: model manifest change diff, tokenizer normalization patch, canary node logs, decode traces. We saw token_id frequency shifts at the first-subtoken position for several common tokens used in evaluation prompts. Weight binary checksums matched expected build artifacts but the packaging job included tokenizer metadata file with a different normalization mapping than the previous release. Log traces showed decodes returning eos where previously there were continuation tokens; beam and sampling parameters unchanged. No kernel selection changes detected during rollout. KV cache contents had entries referencing kv-prefix hashes that included tokenizer-metadata-version; mismatch could cause cache hits that are no longer compatible resulting in decoding artifacts.
root_cause: Packaging error: tokenizer metadata file (normalization map) from an experimental branch was accidentally included in the release bundle that also contained a weight merge. The tokenizer change was incompatible with the combined cached KV entries on canary nodes, resulting in stale prefix/KV cache hits with mismatched token id expectations and premature EOS emission.
immediate_mitigation: 1) Scoped rollback of canary to previous manifest (v2025-09-28z) to stop bad outputs. 2) Targeted prefix/KV cache flush on canary nodes to invalidate stale entries tied to tokenizer metadata. 3) Disabled tokenizer normalization flag in rollout pipeline until packaging issue confirmed. 4) Increased canary isolation gates (traffic -> 0.2% until validation checklist complete).
longer_term_actions: 1) Add pre-release packaging validation that verifies tokenizer metadata checksum is identical across all artifacts for a release. 2) Extend canary smoke-checks to include token_id distribution and eos-rate divergence tests. 3) Modify cache key composition to include tokenizer metadata version to avoid cross-version hits. 4) Add a CI step that runs a mini-decode test on a seeded prompt set to catch eos/truncation regressions. 5) Create a post-deploy checklist requiring cross-check of manifest diffs and tokenizer files when weights change.
runbook_changes_draft:
- When performing weight merges: verify tokenizer metadata parity across artifacts and record tokenizer-version in manifest.
- Add a canary-specific preflight: run 100 representative prompts and assert median length deviation < 5% and eos-rate < 2x baseline.
- If eos spike detected: 1) temporarily reroute canary traffic to previous manifest; 2) flush prefix/KV cache for nodes in canary pool; 3) if KV cache cannot be flushed fast enough, scale canary down and schedule controlled rollback.
- Communicate rollback decision to product and solutions-engineering within 30 minutes.

open_questions:
- How did experimental tokenizer metadata enter the release bundle (CI gap or manual override)?
- Are there any other runtimes or regions still serving requests with mismatched metadata?
- Can we safely change cache key composition without a widespread cache invalidation penalty?

notes_for_oncall: If you see sudden eos spikes during a rollout: check manifest diffs first for tokenizer or encoding metadata changes. If tokenizer metadata changed, prioritize targeted KV/prefix cache invalidation and canary rollback rather than toggling runtime sampling flags. Preserve logs and sample decodes from affected canary nodes and attach to the incident ticket.
postmortem_severity: P2 - degraded quality on limited canary cohort, mitigated quickly, follow-up required
